claims.text: The hardest call in most work is not what to do next but when to stop; past the point of diminishing returns, more work is not more value.
claims.quote: The hardest call in most work is not what to do next but when to stop.

claims.text: The article follows a voice memo recorded after Agency is not a yes, which is the one to read first, and its examples are from the owner's career in application security and as a CISO, with the people not named.
claims.quote: The examples are from my own career, mostly in application security and as a CISO; the people in them are not named.

claims.text: Variability, the ability to try different things and go in directions nobody asked for, is a better name than hallucination and is what makes these systems special; but an entity that can go anywhere has no natural reason to stop anywhere.
claims.quote: An entity that can go anywhere has no natural reason to stop anywhere.

claims.text: A friend said that as a CISO the owner would not care about half of what he cared about in AppSec; from the board some of what seemed urgent was not the most important thing.
claims.quote: when you become a CISO, you will not care about half of what you care about now

claims.text: Much of what we call seniority is perspective: having the bigger picture and being able to move between the tactical and the strategic, and the bigger picture is mostly what tells you when to stop.
claims.quote: And the bigger picture is mostly what tells you when to stop.

claims.text: When security became proactive, the best teams treated it as an engineering problem, a class of bug, and almost every security issue at that level comes down to a practice a good team simply does.
claims.quote: almost every security issue at that level can be brought down to a practice a good team simply does

claims.text: Security champions once debated whether GUIDs were random enough; a version 4 UUID has 122 random bits, around 5.3 x 10^36 values, guessing one is not a realistic attack, and there was no plausible path from a predictable GUID to harm.
claims.quote: A version 4 UUID has 122 random bits

value.unit: random bits in a version 4 UUID

claims.text: A movie plot, in the phrase Bruce Schneier popularised, is a dramatic threat we imagine instead of the ordinary ones that happen; real attacks are mostly someone asking someone to run this, install that, or hand over a key.
claims.quote: It was a movie plot, in the phrase Bruce Schneier popularised for the dramatic threats we imagine instead of the ordinary ones that happen.

claims.text: What the owner found himself doing as a CISO was giving people permission to take risks: perspective, not common sense, about who the attackers are, what else is in place and what is being protected.
claims.quote: What I found myself doing, in that meeting and in many others across the business, was giving people permission to take risks.

claims.text: Development teams hitting every KPI while the business did not move is the example most relevant to agents; when a measure becomes a target, in Marilyn Strathern's phrasing of Goodhart's law, it ceases to be a good measure.
claims.quote: I was in meetings where the development teams were hitting every KPI, delivering everything, and the business was not moving.

claims.text: A Wardley map tells you which phase each part of the business is in: when exploring, polish is waste and knowing when to stop is the most important skill; for a commodity being town-planned, the same polish may be right.
claims.quote: If you are still exploring, still trying to find what makes the business accelerate, polish is waste and the most important skill is knowing when to stop.

claims.text: The call not to fix this bug, not to build that feature, not to improve what is already good enough is often harder than doing the work and belongs to whoever has the context, a person or an agent that has been given it.
claims.quote: That call is often harder than doing the work, and it belongs to whoever has the context: a person, or an agent that has been given it.

claims.text: The best feedback loop for knowing what is good enough is shipping often and early, and observability is how you find out whether the work changed anything outside the team.
claims.quote: The best feedback loop I know for it is shipping, often and early.

claims.text: An LLM has a far wider range than a person and can keep going: asked to fix a small thing it fixes a bigger one, sees twenty things wrong and tries all of them, without knowing nineteen do not matter.
claims.quote: You ask it to fix a small thing and it fixes a bigger one, because it can.

claims.text: There is nothing uniquely agentic about this: C. Northcote Parkinson observed in 1955 that work expands to fill the time available, and past controls like fixed team sizes were artificial and draconian because the real problems were communication and direction.
claims.quote: The real problems were communication and direction, not the number.

claims.text: The better answer is constraints that carry the bigger picture rather than rules that only forbid; Dan Ward's FIRE, fast, inexpensive, restrained and elegant, is one name for that attitude and a doctrine on wardley-maps.sgit.ai.
claims.quote: The better answer is constraints that carry the bigger picture, rather than rules that only forbid.

claims.text: Direction: briefs that explain the thinking and the objective, not only the task, so an agent can judge what matters.
claims.quote: briefs that explain the thinking and the objective, not only the task, so an agent can judge what matters

claims.text: A mandate: an Agent Behaviour Policy and tools that only reach what the job needs, so the agent's universe of the possible is the size of the job.
claims.quote: so the agent's universe of the possible is the size of the job

claims.text: Memory with the bigger picture: vaults and pages that hold the strategy, the threats and the history, so the perspective a senior person carries in their head is in the agent's context too.
claims.quote: so the perspective a senior person carries in their head is in the agent's context too

claims.text: Graphs that narrow the scope: semantic and flow graphs say what connects to what and therefore what is in and out of scope for this step.
claims.quote: semantic and flow graphs say what connects to what, and therefore what is in and out of scope for this step

claims.text: A stop named in advance: for an agent that is a token budget on the step, set before it starts, with the stopping point named while it is still cheap to name.
claims.quote: For an agent that is a token budget on the step, set before it starts.

claims.text: The agent team runs each agent for one step of up to twelve minutes: read state, do one kind of work, write state, stop.
claims.quote: read state, do one kind of work, write state, stop

claims.text: A reviewer with agency, someone with the context to say good enough or not this, that, and shipping, so the users answer the question of whether it mattered.
claims.quote: A reviewer with agency: someone with the context to say "good enough", or "not this, that"

claims.text: None of these constraints is a rule that says do less; each puts the bigger picture where the decision is made.
claims.quote: None of these is a rule that says "do less".

claims.text: Where to start: name the stop before you start, write down which phase you are in, give the agent the bigger picture, measure the needle not only the KPI, one kind of work per step, and give explicit permission to leave things undone.
claims.quote: Give explicit permission to leave things undone, and write down what was left and why.

claims.text: The people in the examples are not named; the UUID figures are from RFC 9562, Parkinson's sentence from The Economist of 19 November 1955, Goodhart's phrasing Marilyn Strathern's from 1997, and FIRE the title of Dan Ward's 2014 book.
claims.quote: The people in the examples are not named.
